notes: Company background: mid-sized e-discovery provider focused on EU regulators and large financial institutions.
Primary problem: current search stack (Elasticsearch + off-the-shelf embeddings) has high tail latency and poor precision for legal queries; lots of manual review time.
Indexing scale: initial corpus ~20M documents (compressed), expect growth 2x in 12 months; average doc size 8k tokens, many PDFs and nested attachments.
Throughput & latency targets: 500 qps peak for internal user workflows; p95 end-to-end RAG (embed + ANN + rerank) target <= 250ms, ideal <=150ms for prioritized flows.
Cost sensitivity: procurement wants < $0.03/query average for production RAG workflows (embedding + ANN + lightweight reranker); willingness to pay more for low-latency SLAs.
Model preferences: open models preferred (Llama-family quantized); want option to run cross-encoder reranker (smaller T5-like) locally in VPC for PII-sensitive reranking.
Routing/fallback needs: multi-tier routing (fast cheap embed-only fallback; high-accuracy rerank on dedicated capacity); automatic fallback when cross-encoder capacity exceeded.
Security/compliance notes: EU data residency mandatory; audit logging for all token-level events; retention policy (immutable logs) for 7 years; SSO via SAML; want per-customer key control (HSM).

Operational asks: ability to precompute and persist embeddings, TTL policies for frequently mutated docs, incremental index updates with minimal re-embedding, and cold-start warmup for new model variants.
Pilot ask: 8-week pilot in customer VPC with access to Dedicated nodes + private control plane; success metrics: latency p95 <250ms, recall@10 >= 0.82 vs current baseline, cost per query <= $0.03.
Quote from head of search: "We need deterministic latency and forensic audit trails for every search. If you can show that in a VPC pilot, procurement will move fast."

Tech stack notes: current infra uses vector DB (self-hosted FAISS/HNSW) sharded across 8 nodes; ingestion pipeline in Airflow; interested in Redwood's KV caching and automatic batching to reduce token cost.

Risk flags: procurement requires vendor SOC2 Type II + ISO27001 documentation plus a clear manifest of what data flows to Redwood-managed services. Prefer private deployment to avoid third-party data egress concerns.

Suggested Redwood positioning: highlight Private deployment (VPC + on-prem connector), audit logging retention controls, KMS/HSM integration, cost controls (Optimize recommendations), and deterministic routing/fallback policies. Emphasize support for large indexes and incremental re-embed.
